chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked him about one who did not fast the three days and fasting is hard on him, is there a ransom (fidyah) for him? He said: 'A mud of food for each day.'

key_terms.مُدٌّ: A specific unit of volume measurement for food

ai.seo_question: What is the fidyah for missing three days of fasting due to hardship?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific compensation (fidyah) for those who miss three days of fasting due to genuine hardship, prescribing one mud of food per day. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on proportionality and ease, distinguishing this partial compensation from the full expiation required for other fasting violations, thereby reflecting the practical application of divine mercy in Islamic law.
